svg.text: A. HIDDEN TILT STRIP (the build's PRIMARY system -- required to drive the ARCH slats)
P pivot pin (1/4"), slat centerline
D drive pin (3/16")
at 3/8" offset = CRANK ARM
vertical strip, slides UP/DOWN
only (captive in stile groove)
slotted hole engages D
strip travel ~5/8" over the
+/-60 working range
HOW IT WORKS: each slat has TWO pins in its center-stile end:
the PIVOT pin (P) on the centerline that it rotates on, and a
DRIVE pin (D) offset 3/8" from P. D sits in a slotted hole in
a thin vertical strip that can only slide up/down in a groove
in the stile. Push the strip DOWN: every D is dragged down and
every slat cranks about its P in unison -- closed. Pull UP:
closed the other way. The slot lets D swing sideways as it
arcs. Because every slat has the SAME 3/8" crank arm, slat
LENGTH is irrelevant: the arch slats rotate in perfect unison
with the straight ones. Friction from the spring pins holds
any position. WORKING RANGE +/-60 deg: the slats SEAL
by overlap at ~56 deg, so the pins never over-travel.
BUY, DON'T MAKE: commercial "invisible tilt" aluminum strips
(slotted 1/8" x 3/4") + louver pins are standard replacement
parts. Groove the center stile 5/32" x 13/16", OFFSET
7/16" toward the FRONT face -- the bar must run forward of
the pivot line so it clears the pivot pins.
B. TRADITIONAL VISIBLE CENTER ROD (the classic look -- reference photo)
A wood rod hangs in FRONT of the slats, attached by INTERLOCKED SCREW EYES (per reference video): one small eye in the front of each
slat, one at the matching mark on the rod, opened with pliers, hooked through, closed. Rod down = front edges rotate down = closed; rod up
= closed the other way. Pivots per the same video: 1/4" x 2" hardwood DOWEL PINS glued 1" into each slat end, riding in stile/ring holes.
Hold-open: ONE tension slat per bank, flat-end screws driven through the frame into its ends -- tighten to stiffen. Carve a clearance slot
where the rod crosses a rail so slats close fully.
THE ARCH FINDING: the eyes need a common VERTICAL line, not slat midpoints. A rod line 2-3/4" from the center stile crosses EVERY slat
including the whole arch bank (shortest C-slat is 3-13/16"), so visible rods CAN drive the full leaf: one rod per bank on that line, trimmed
just above the C12 link (verify ring clearance at full tilt on the test article). Mirrored on the other leaf, the two rods flank the center split.
